subsystems.name: Film deposition
subsystems.role: lays down the superconducting metal stack that carries currents and sets qubit coherence.
parts: molecular-beam or atomic-layer deposition for the tunnel barrier

subsystems.name: Junction definition
subsystems.role: creates the Josephson junction — the non-linear element that makes a qubit a qubit.
parts: electron-beam lithography for the resist bridge
shadow evaporation of aluminium at two angles
controlled oxidation to form the AlOx barrier

subsystems.name: Patterning and resonators
subsystems.role: shapes readout resonators, capacitors and control lines to tight dimensional tolerance.

subsystems.name: Interconnect and routing
subsystems.role: gets many control and readout signals on and off a dense chip without crosstalk.
parts: flip-chip indium bump bonding to a carrier wafer

subsystems.name: Wafer-scale test
subsystems.role: measures every device on the wafer so process drift can be caught and corrected.

subsystems.name: Process design kit
subsystems.role: the interface that lets an outside team design a chip without owning the line.
parts: device models and electromagnetic simulation decks
layout templates for qubits, resonators and wiring

buildSteps.title: Define the stack and design rules
buildSteps.detail: The foundry fixes which metals, thicknesses and minimum feature sizes designers may use, and publishes them as a kit.

buildSteps.title: Design and submit a layout
buildSteps.detail: An external team places qubits, couplers and readout lines in a layout file, simulates the electromagnetics, and submits it for a scheduled multi-project wafer run.

buildSteps.title: Deposit base metallisation
buildSteps.detail: Niobium or tantalum is sputtered onto a 200 mm or 300 mm silicon wafer, then patterned and etched into resonators, capacitors and wiring.

buildSteps.title: Write the junctions
buildSteps.detail: Electron-beam lithography defines a resist bridge over each junction site; aluminium is evaporated from two angles with a controlled oxidation step in between, so an AlOx tunnel barrier forms.

buildSteps.title: Add airbridges and vias
buildSteps.detail: Raised metal bridges cross over signal lines to suppress unwanted microwave modes, and through-silicon vias open paths to the back of the wafer.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the chip stack
buildSteps.detail: The qubit wafer is flip-chip bonded to a carrier that holds readout and control routing, using indium bumps aligned to a few micrometres.

buildSteps.title: Test across the wafer
buildSteps.detail: Junction resistances are mapped at room temperature to infer qubit frequencies; sample chips go into dilution refrigerators for coherence and gate-fidelity checks.

buildSteps.title: Feed statistics back into the kit
buildSteps.detail: Wafer maps of junction resistance and frequency are used to tighten design rules and retarget the process, so the next run lands closer to specification.

prerequisites.tech: Superconducting thin-film deposition at CMOS scale
prerequisites.why: niobium, aluminium and tantalum films with low microwave loss are routine on 200 mm and 300 mm tooling.

prerequisites.tech: Sub-100 nm electron-beam lithography with precise overlay
prerequisites.why: junction area directly sets qubit frequency, so placement errors translate into device failure.
measuring thousands of qubits below 1 K is slow and expensive, so yield is inferred rather than measured.
published kits exist but cover a narrow set of devices and change as the physics understanding moves.
wiring thousands of coaxial lines into a dilution refrigerator is impractical; multiplexed or cold electronics are needed.

pathway.milestone: Multi-project wafer runs and a handful of dedicated qubit lines, including long-running superconducting fab work at national laboratories and industrial 300 mm efforts
pathway.unlocks: university and startup teams can build qubits without owning a fab.

pathway.milestone: Standardised kits with a validated library of qubits, couplers and readout resonators
pathway.unlocks: design reuse, the way digital chip design became modular decades ago.

pathway.milestone: Statistical process control that reliably targets qubit frequency across a full wafer
pathway.unlocks: wafers of near-identical qubits, a prerequisite for error correction at scale.

pathway.milestone: Integration of qubits with cryogenic control and readout layers on the same stack
pathway.unlocks: systems with thousands of physical qubits and manageable wiring.
